issues.t: Front crossmember rusts and control arm can break loose
issues.sym: The truck pulls hard to one side when braking, the steering feels loose or wanders, clunks from the front end, a front tire rubs or wobbles. In the worst cases a lower control arm tears away from the frame.
issues.why: The front suspension crossmember, which holds the lower control arms, rusts badly in road-salt states. GM started a special coverage program (number 06186) after NHTSA looked into control arms separating.
issues.next: Have the crossmember inspected now, especially if you live where roads are salted. If you feel pulling or clunking, stop driving and have it towed. Ask a Chevrolet dealer whether your VIN was covered by the program.

issues.t: Front axle clunks or 4WD pops out of gear
issues.sym: A harsh clunk or pop from the front axle, or 4WD that slips in and out and won't stay engaged.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for a harsh clunk from the front axle, and an owner reports the front differential case was redesigned. The front differential case, actuator and side bearings can need replacing.
issues.next: Have the front differential and 4WD actuator checked before it gets worse. Avoid using 4WD on dry pavement.

issues.t: Hard to shift transfer case from 2H to 4H
issues.sym: The 4WD lever is very stiff moving from 2H to 4H, especially the first time or while moving.
issues.why: GM issued several bulletins about high shift effort in the transfer case on four-wheel-drive Trackers.
issues.next: Shift into 4H at low speed while driving straight. If it stays stiff, a dealer can apply the bulletin fix.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slips or downshifts on its own
issues.sym: The automatic shifts down unexpectedly, slips, or the torque converter clutch cycles on and off. The cooling fan may also be noisy.
issues.why: GM issued a diagnostic bulletin for intermittent downshifts, slipping and torque converter clutch problems on these models.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and condition, then have a shop diagnose it using the GM bulletin before it causes wear.

issues.t: Engine overheats
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, steam or coolant smell from the engine bay, or the heater blows cold.
issues.why: Overheating is the top reported problem for the 2003 Tracker, and repairs are often costly. Coolant leaks, a failing radiator or water pump, or a blown head gasket can all cause it.
issues.next: Pull over and shut the engine off if the gauge goes into the red. Have the cooling system pressure-tested; driving hot can warp the cylinder head.

issues.t: Engine runs rough or dies when hot
issues.sym: The engine runs rough, stalls or stops running once fully warmed up, sometimes after a long drive.
issues.why: Owners report rough running and stalling when hot at high mileage. A failing sensor, ignition part or fuel supply problem can cause it.
issues.next: Note when it happens and have the codes read and fuel pressure checked while the engine is hot.

issues.t: Engine shakes when coming to a stop
issues.sym: Strong shaking or vibration through the vehicle as you slow to a stop or sit at idle.
issues.why: Owners report heavy shaking at idle at high mileage. Worn engine mounts, a dirty throttle body or misfires are common causes.
issues.next: Have the engine mounts inspected and check for misfire codes.

issues.t: Ticking noise from the engine
issues.sym: A light tick from the engine, cold or hot.
issues.why: GM revised its bulletin on this tick noise several times between 2000 and 2003. The dealer follows the bulletin to find the source.
issues.next: Check the oil level first. If the noise is new or getting louder, have it checked and mention GM's tick-noise bulletin.

issues.t: Slow start or no-start in very cold weather
issues.sym: In very cold weather the engine cranks slowly, cranks without starting, or starts and dies.
issues.why: GM ran an emissions service campaign on 1999 Trackers for cold-weather no-starts and later issued another bulletin for slow or no starts in extreme cold.
issues.next: Check your VIN with a Chevrolet dealer for the campaign. A healthy battery and a block heater help in severe cold.

issues.t: 2.5L V6 hard to start or won't start at times
issues.sym: The V6 cranks longer than normal or sometimes won't start.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for intermittent no-start and hard-start on the 2.5L V6.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the shop to check GM's bulletin for the 2.5L V6.

issues.t: Ignition key sticks or binds
issues.sym: The key binds in the accessory position, sticks when turning to lock, or is hard to turn or remove, mostly on automatics.
issues.why: GM issued many bulletins on Tracker ignition locks and keys binding in accessory, and on ignition lock replacements.
issues.next: Don't force the key. A dealer or locksmith can replace the lock cylinder or switch; bring all your keys.

issues.t: Serpentine belt squeals or frays
issues.sym: A squeal from the engine, especially on startup, or a belt that looks frayed or jumps off its grooves.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins on frayed serpentine belts, belts jumping grooves and belt squeal.
issues.next: Replace a frayed belt right away; if it comes off you lose charging and power steering. Have the pulleys checked for alignment.

issues.t: Driveline vibration at 35–60 mph
issues.sym: A vibration through the floor or seat between about 35 and 60 mph.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for driveshaft vibration in this speed range.
issues.next: Have the tires balanced and the driveshaft and U-joints checked. The dealer can apply the bulletin fix.

issues.t: Brake pedal pulsates from rotor corrosion
issues.sym: The brake pedal or steering wheel pulses or vibrates when braking, especially at higher speeds.
issues.why: Corrosion between the wheel hub and brake rotor makes the rotor run out of true. GM issued bulletins for this and for rear brake pulsation.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured. Resurfacing or replacing the rotors and cleaning the hub face fixes it.

issues.t: Front end creaks or pops over bumps and in turns
issues.sym: Creaking, squeaking or popping from the front suspension over bumps or when turning tightly.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for front-end creaking and popping, and owners report squeaks when turning.
issues.next: Have the front suspension checked. Rule out the crossmember rust problem first, since it can also cause noises.

issues.t: Convertible soft top leaks water
issues.sym: Water drips inside around the soft top edges, especially in rain or car washes.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for water leaks on the convertible top.
issues.next: Have the top seals and fit checked. Dry the carpet quickly to prevent mold and rust.

issues.t: Water gets into main fuse box and corrodes it
issues.sym: Odd electrical faults: lights, accessories or gauges that work on and off.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for water getting into the main junction (fuse) box and causing corrosion.
issues.next: Have the fuse box checked for water and corrosion. Cleaning, resealing or replacing it stops the faults.

issues.t: Front windows bind or tip forward
issues.sym: A front window tips forward, binds in its track or makes noise when going up or down.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for front windows tipping forward and binding in the channel.
issues.next: Have the window channel and regulator adjusted. Don't keep forcing a stuck window.

issues.t: Door handles break
issues.sym: An inside or outside door handle snaps off and the door won't open from that side.
issues.why: Owners report door handles breaking easily on these years.
issues.next: Replace the handle. Open the door from the other side until it is fixed.

issues.t: Instrument cluster or lights flicker
issues.sym: The instrument cluster, interior lights or headlamps flicker.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for flickering cluster, interior and headlamps.
issues.next: Have the charging system and grounds checked. The dealer can follow the bulletin.

issues.t: Stiff gas pedal and harsh automatic shifts
issues.sym: The gas pedal takes more effort than normal, the automatic shifts hard or late, or cruise control downshifts and is slow to upshift.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for high accelerator pedal effort with hard shifts and for cruise control shift behavior.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the throttle linkage and apply the bulletins.

issues.t: Rattle in neutral with clutch released
issues.sym: On manual trucks, a rattle in low gear or neutral that stops when you press the clutch pedal.
issues.why: Owners report this rattle on manual trucks. Worn input-shaft bearings or clutch parts are typical causes.
issues.next: Have a shop check the transmission oil level and listen to the clutch and gearbox before it gets worse.

issues.t: Heater blows from the wrong vents or quits
issues.sym: Weak or no heat, or warm air comes from the dash vents instead of the floor.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for heat not being directed correctly, and owners report heater cores failing.
issues.next: Check the coolant level. If it is full, have the heater blend and mode doors and the heater core checked.

issues.t: Fuel gauge stuck after filling up
issues.sym: After fueling, the gauge stays around a quarter tank or reads wrong.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for the fuel gauge reading incorrectly after fueling.
issues.next: Track miles since your last fill-up until it is fixed so you don't run out. A dealer can follow the bulletin.

issues.t: Check engine light from loose or worn gas cap
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with no change in how the engine runs.
issues.why: The most common Tracker problem on RepairPal is a gas cap that doesn't seal, which sets an evaporative emissions code.
issues.next: Tighten the cap until it clicks. If the light stays on after a few drives, replace the cap and have the codes read.

issues.t: Creak from right rear wheel opening on 4-door
issues.sym: A creak from the right rear wheel area of 4-door models, often over bumps.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for creaking from the right rear wheel opening on some 4-door models.
issues.next: A dealer can apply the bulletin fix; it is a noise, not a safety issue.

issues.t: Steering shaft coupling may crack (safety campaign)
issues.sym: Possible looseness or clunking in the steering. A cracked coupling could cause loss of steering control.
issues.why: A safety campaign was issued to replace steering column shaft couplings that could crack.
issues.next: Check your VIN with a Chevrolet dealer for open campaigns. The repair is free.

issues.t: Windshield may not be held in properly (safety campaign)
issues.sym: No warning signs. In a crash the windshield may not stay in place as required.
issues.why: Some windshields were not installed to meet the federal retention standard. A campaign was issued, with a renotification in 2000.
issues.next: Check your VIN with a Chevrolet dealer; the windshield is reinstalled or replaced for free.
